paragraphs: Rav Shemen bar Abba the priest. R' Hanina told him to marry one of his relatives, Shmuel's daughters of priestly descent, who had been captured and redeemed: Ketubbot 23a. See Rav Mari, the son of Shmuel's daughter. He said in Rav Idi bar Gershon's name. R' Zeira said to him: Hullin 98a. R' Hiyya bar Abba was perhaps his brother. He was R' Yohanan's pupil: Shabbat 60b, 61a. He said in R' Yohanan's name: beginning of the first chapter of Megillah; Avodah Zarah 28a. R' Yohanan was distressed about ordaining him because he was not with them to be ordained. R' Shimon ben Zerud and one with him—who was it? R' Yonatan ben Akhmai: they ordained the one who was with them, and did not ordain the one who was not with them. Sanhedrin 14a. R' Yohanan held that he should not eat the testicles still attached to the animal’s body, because “Do not forsake your mother's teaching.” Rashi explains: your locality's custom, for you are from Babylonia, where they prohibit it; Hullin 93b. “I was standing before R' Yohanan in the study hall on the intermediate festival days, and he removed his nails with his teeth and threw them away.” Infer three things from this: Mo'ed Katan 18a. “R' Yohanan said to Rav Shemen”: Sanhedrin 5b. It appears to be Rav Shemen bar Abba, who lived in his generation. He said to Rav Pappa, “According to you, who said …”: Pesahim 59, beginning of side b. This requires examination: he lived in R' Yohanan's time, long before Rav Pappa. Did he live so long? It appears that the Rav Shemen who spoke to Rav Pappa is the Rav Shemen mentioned in Rav Ashi's generation; see his entry and immediately below. Or it was Rav Pappa the Elder.
